verdict.rationale: Angular's docs describe built-in fine-grained reactive state via Angular Signals and a first-party dependency injection system, both core framework primitives, so no third-party library is needed for reactive state. The evidence consists only of homepage taglines, though, and never shows these primitives being used for app-wide shared state. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of a global or shared-state pattern (e.g. signals in injectable singleton services), detail on state APIs beyond a one-line claim, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
